championship.scoring: Six cars, 10 laps per race; F1 points 25-18-15-12-10-8 for classified finishers; ranked by total points over three races, ties by the last race. Race 1's grid by lot, later grids by the previous result.

checkpoint.measure: Pace score, ratio to the reference program (1.0 = reference)

names: Vehicle dynamics: planning at the grip limit

skills.name: Completes a valid lap
skills.real: The basic requirement of a time trial: pull away from rest and drive a full lap without all four wheels past the white line, the barrier or driving the wrong way; only then does the lap count.
skills.measure: Baseline scenario (the official time trial's run 1: standing start, two timed laps): runs with the match set / runs. The Checkpoint Evaluations read the same field.

skills.name: Laps fast enough
skills.real: A2RL / IAC cars run at the grip limit; the lap time comes from how much grip is used and where the car brakes.
skills.measure: Baseline scenario: the match record = the platform's plan lap time / the best valid lap (the reference reads about 0.94; no valid lap scores 0.2), median over seeds.

skills.name: Carries speed through tight corners
skills.real: Lap time is won in the slow corners: a slightly slow entry costs the whole straight after it.
skills.measure: Every passage of the two tightest corners in the baseline (official start) + scenario hairpin: over the corners passed cleanly, the lowest speed in the corner / the platform plan's lowest speed there (the scenario record and / v_plan_min), pooled median. Gate: ≥ 2 clean corners.

skills.name: Takes a hairpin at the limit, cleanly
skills.real: Before a hairpin the car brakes from over 250 km/h to about 90 km/h: braking point, steering and throttle have to agree, and a little late means the barrier. Opus kickoff:1 hit the barrier at the 974 m hairpin in its Checkpoint Evaluations.
skills.measure: Pooled from two sources: (1) every passage of the two tightest corners in the baseline (official start, two laps): clean = no new track-limit call and no DNF up to 200 m after the exit, and the lowest corner speed ≥ 0.8 × the plan's; (2) scenario hairpin: a flying start 250 m before one of the two tightest corners at the reference plan's speed (held until the program's first act), ending 200 m after the exit; clean = reaches the end with no barrier / wrong way / track-limit call and within 1.25 × the reference's time on the same seed and corner. A unit that leaves the road before reaching the corner after the flying start gives no reading (the program lost itself; see findings).

skills.name: No incident over a lap
skills.real: A2RL teams write their own traction, braking and steering control; one barrier contact is a DNF.
skills.measure: Baseline scenario + Checkpoint Evaluations: of the runs that pulled away (≥ 100 m), the share with no barrier, wrong way or track-limit call (, track_limits, progress_m).

skills.name: Catches a slide
skills.real: A kerb or a bump can snap the rear out; a driver (or autonomy stack) has a few tenths of a second to counter-steer and lift to save it.
skills.measure: Scenario slide: the hairpin start; a third of the way round the corner the world adds 2.0 m/s of sideways velocity towards the outside and 0.25 rad/s of yaw rate into the turn; recovered = reaches the end with no barrier / wrong way / track-limit call. Gate: speed at the kick ≥ 0.8 × the reference's at the same corner (crawling does not count).

skills.name: Steady steering
skills.real: Sawing at the wheel at speed upsets the tyres, costs speed and can lose the car.
skills.measure: Every unit of the scenarios: direction changes of the applied steering angle (0.004 rad hysteresis) per second above 20 m/s, median over baseline + hairpin. Gate: the program completes a valid lap or a clean corner.

skills.name: Commands keep coming
skills.real: At 80 m/s 20 ms is 1.6 m; real cars command at the order of 100 Hz.
skills.measure: The world records the step of every applied act: the gap between consecutive acts while above 5 m/s, p95 per unit (the scenario record, in 10 ms steps), median over the scenarios.

skills.name: Keeps the double yellow
skills.real: A double-yellow sector has a speed limit and speeding is penalised. The official run 2 has a 250 m, 100 km/h double yellow.
skills.measure: Scenario yellow: the official standing start; a 250 m, 100 km/h double yellow starts 120 m after the line (announced in from the first step); the unit ends 150 m after it, two units; kept = no yellow_violation and a sector mean ≥ 80 km/h.

off.name: Onboard camera perception
off.why: There is no other car in a time trial, so camera perception cannot be read. Scenario alongside (a car beside yours) was not built: the time-trial observation has no other car and only the camera would show it, which tests something the task never asked for; it needs the passing / race tasks.

off.name: Race strategy (candidate)
off.why: Exists only in the multi-car race and not in the Checkpoint Evaluation.

off.name: Adaptive
off.why: Not declared on the card; read across checkpoints (the growth curve).

notes.challenge: A 750 kg, 405 kW single-seater through a drive-by-wire interface. The program plans the racing line and speed at the grip limit and acts on time at real speed.

achieved.text: No program obeys the yellow flag: the frozen programs drove 180 to 196 km/h through a 100 km/h sector.
Every audited racing program was hand-written control code; none loaded a learned model.
